name: policy_drift_memory_v1
description: A deterministic agent-memory benchmark for support and operations agents that must retain current instructions while suppressing stale ones.

events.text: Acme support starts with daily incident digests in Slack at 08:00 UTC. Include customer names and raw ticket excerpts.

facts.value: customer names and raw ticket excerpts allowed

events.text: Acme privacy review supersedes the old digest policy. Never include customer names or raw ticket excerpts; use anonymized ticket IDs only.
The daily incident digest time moves from 08:00 UTC to 09:30 UTC so the EU support lead can review it first.
Escalations for Acme should go to PagerDuty service ACME-EU-P1, not the old shared ops rotation.
Bravo Research wants an agent to track experiment notes. Initial reports can use full participant names for convenience.
IRB guidance overrides earlier reporting. Bravo reports must use participant codes only and must flag consent changes since the last session.

facts.value: flag consent changes since the last session

events.text: Bravo moves the weekly report owner from Data Science to the Clinical Ops reviewer.
Cobalt release agents should publish readiness summaries to email. The initial launch train is beta-4.
Cobalt changes the launch train to rc-1. Do not mention beta-4 in current release recommendations.
Cobalt release summaries now go to the #release-readiness Slack channel instead of email.

queries.question: What is the current digest time and privacy rule for Acme support?
Where should Acme P1 escalations go now?
What privacy rule should Bravo reports follow?
Who owns the Bravo weekly report now, and what consent detail must be flagged?
required: flag consent changes since the last session
